title: T1597.002 — Search Closed Sources - Purchase Technical Data
subtitle: Watch purchased records become a chosen entry point, and see the two echoes the SOC can still catch.
aria: Animated diagram of an attacker buying WHOIS history, passive DNS, and certificate data from a technical data platform to map a target company's forgotten assets, while the SOC receives a vendor bulk-query alert. A written version of every step follows below the diagram.

steps.title: Buy API credits
steps.caption: The broker funds a technical-data platform account with a few hundred dollars. No target name is attached yet, so nothing looks special.
steps.defender: Data platforms keep API audit logs. A clause at renewal can give you alerts when your domains are queried in bulk.

steps.title: Pull WHOIS history
steps.caption: WHOIS history for the target's main domain shows the 2013 registrant, a 2014 re-registration, and two retired brand names still connected to the company.
steps.defender: Watch retired brand and acquisition domains too - attackers harvest them from exactly this data.

steps.title: Query passive DNS
steps.caption: Passive DNS returns every hostname that ever resolved for the target: today's site, plus a long tail of test, staging, and VPN hosts.
steps.defender: Your own mirror query shows the same list. If it surprises you, it will surprise an attacker less.

steps.title: Find the forgotten assets
steps.caption: Cross-checking shows vpn-old.target.example still resolves, and a certificate for it was renewed last year. The target's CMDB has no record of it.
steps.defender: 'Resolving but unknown' must be a P1 finding. This exact gap is what the broker is paying to find.

steps.title: Pull certificate history
steps.caption: Certificate records reveal internal naming conventions - hq-vpn01, core-fs02 patterns - that future lookalike domains can copy verbatim.
steps.defender: Stop issuing public certificates with internal names. CT logs make them public forever.

steps.title: Assemble the map
steps.caption: Everything merges into one picture: 38 assets, one clearly abandoned, one still serving a login page. The target's own inventory lists 11.
steps.defender: A monthly ASM-versus-CMDB diff closes this gap on your side. Freshness beats perfection.

fields.detail: Everything merges into one picture: 38 assets, one clearly abandoned, one still serving a login page

detection.label: Partial signal
detection.detail: A weak signal exists but is not yet a confirmed alert.

steps.title: Check the quiet door
steps.caption: A single harmless-looking HTTPS request confirms the old VPN portal is alive and serving a login page. The broker now has a product to sell.
steps.defender: A sinkhole or logger on retired IP ranges turns this probe into a signal you can actually see.

detection.label: Alert raised
detection.detail: The SOC has enough evidence to open an incident.

steps.title: The SOC's echoes
steps.caption: The SOC sees none of the queries in its own logs. Its two echoes: a vendor bulk-query alert about the domain, and its own ASM mirror diff - if someone wired both up.
steps.defender: Run the attacker's queries on yourself first, and the purchased map returns nothing they did not already fix.
